newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Mixed signals from NZ First Maori MPs.
newsitem.headline: Mixed signals from NZ First Maori MPs.

text.p: New Zealand First's Maori MPs were sending mixed signals as they gathered on Tuesday for the key meeting to decide the party's coalition partner, with one saying the Labour Party had failed Maori in the past.

Tutekawa Wyllie, MP for the Southern Maori seat Te Tai Tonga, acknowledged his own constituency supporters favoured Labour as a coalition partner. "Yes, my people have an expectation of me to go Labour."
Wyllie said he would make the decision in the best interests of the country. Asked if that would be with Labour, he said: "It may well be."

Tukuroirangi Morgan, MP for Te Tai Hauauru, told reporters thousands of people in his constituency had deserted Labour for NZ First "because of the Labour Party's apathy and mediocrity. Maori people were sick and tired of being marginalised".

He added: "I've gone back to the people and they have said to me in some respects that the Labour Party is the preference but...it's an even race. We'll weigh up the decision on what will benefit Maori."
New Zealand First won all five seats reserved for Maoris -- previously a stronghold of the Labour Party -- in the October 12 election.

Asked about the influence of leader Winston Peters on the party's choice, Morgan said: "Winston has one vote, I have one vote, and together with the New Zealand First ruling council we will make a measured decision as to what is best for the country, couched with the aspirations of Maori."
